title: Associate
description:
Associate, Corporate

Work location

Toronto, Ontario (hybrid)

About us

For 50 years, NATIONAL has worked alongside organizations as they navigate change, protect reputation, and solve the business challenges that matter most. In Toronto, our Corporate team supports clients across sectors and works closely with colleagues across practices to deliver integrated communications programs, from media relations and stakeholder engagement to issues management, digital, and campaign support. We're looking for an associate who is curious, organized, and ready to roll up their sleeves to help keep great client work moving.

The role

You'll support communications mandates from planning through execution, helping teams bring client work to life while building a strong foundation in client service. Working closely with colleagues across the Toronto office, you'll contribute to day-to-day client activities, assist in developing communications materials, and support the delivery of integrated programs across corporate communications, media relations, public affairs, stakeholder engagement, and digital channels.

This role is ideal for someone early in their career who wants broad agency exposure, enjoys practical execution, and is motivated to learn by doing. You'll be hands-on with research, writing, monitoring, reporting, and coordination, while gaining exposure to a range of clients, sectors, and practice areas.

Key responsibilities

  • Support the day-to-day delivery of integrated communications programs across media relations, stakeholder engagement, public affairs, digital, social, and corporate reputation channels
  • Develop and contribute to high-quality communications materials, including media pitches, press materials, briefing notes, key messages, social media copy, newsletters, client updates, and executive-ready summaries
  • Conduct research, environmental scans, and monitoring across business, media, policy, competitor, stakeholder, and social/digital landscapes to identify insights, trends, risks, and opportunities
  • Support media relations activities, including media list development, journalist research, pitch coordination, coverage tracking, and preparation of media briefing materials
  • Use AI-enabled and digital tools responsibly to support research, content development, brainstorming, summarization, workflow efficiencies, issues tracking, reporting, and audience insights, while applying fact-checking, privacy awareness, and sound judgment
  • Prepare client-facing reports, project updates, and campaign summaries that translate data, media coverage, and engagement metrics into clear, actionable insights
  • Coordinate logistics and project management for meetings, events, stakeholder engagements, internal working sessions, and awareness campaigns, including agendas, briefing materials, vendor coordination, timelines, approvals, budgets, and status documents
  • Support campaign planning, new business proposals, team brainstorming, and cross-practice collaboration while staying current on business, AI, media, and communications trends

Qualifications

  • 2-3 years of experience in public relations, communications, corporate communications, marketing, public affairs, or a related field; agency experience is an asset
  • Post-secondary education in communications, public relations, marketing, journalism, business, political science, or a related discipline
  • Strong writing and editing skills with excellent attention to detail
  • Familiarity with social media platforms, media monitoring tools, and digital communications channels
  • Interest in corporate communications, reputation management, media relations, public affairs, business issues, and integrated campaigns across sectors
  • Comfort using AI-enabled tools, such as ChatGPT, to support research, writing, summarization, and workflow efficiency, with appropriate fact-checking and judgment

Abilities

  • Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail and reliable follow-through
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced environment
  • Proactive, resourceful, and comfortable taking direction while anticipating what needs to happen next
  • Collaborative team player who enjoys supporting different teams, practices, and client files
  • Curious, adaptable, and motivated to continuously learn and grow across sectors and communications disciplines

What we offer

  • Hybrid work environment and a supportive, collegial office culture
  • Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits
  • Broad exposure to client work across the Toronto office and NATIONAL's practice areas
  • Opportunities to work on high-profile mandates with leading organizations across sectors
  • Professional development, coaching, and growth opportunities within a national team, with occasional travel as required by client and team needs

Expected compensation

The expected salary for this role is $50,000-$62,500 CAD. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and internal equity.

How to apply

Submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your interest and fit for the role. If you're ready to build your communications career with Canada's PR Firm, we'd love to hear from you.

NATIONAL is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are dedicated to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Should you require any accommodation during the selection process, please inform us.

A vacancy currently exists for this position. Please note that only candidates selected for further consideration will be contacted. We use artificial intelligence tools to assist in screening, assessing, and selecting applicants for this role. Thank you for considering a career with us.

NATIONAL Public Relations provides creative communications solutions that move people in thought and actions. We bring together a team of 300 seasoned professionals, who are committed to helping organizations of all sizes and in all sectors understand their challenges and opportunities and solve the issues they are facing. For 47 years, NATIONAL has been at the center of issues and industries that matter, leading change for today and tomorrow.

NATIONAL is Canada’s leading public relations firm, with offices in Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Ottawa, Montreal, Quebec City, Saint John, Halifax and St. John’s. Its network includes Time & Space, a leader in media strategy, data analysis, planning and execution.

NATIONAL Public Relations is an AVENIR GLOBAL company, the largest Canadian-owned global communications firm, ranked among the 25 largest in the world with offices in 23 locations across Canada, the U.S., Europe and the Middle East. For more information about NATIONAL, please visit our website or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

title: Conseiller(ère), Relations médias, positionnement corporatif et produits (Remplacement de congé de maternité)
description:
Lieu du travail

Montréal

À propos de nous

Le Cabinet de relations publiques NATIONAL, la plus importante firme-conseil en relations publiques au Canada, accompagne des organisations de premier plan dans la gestion de leurs enjeux de communication, de réputation et de positionnement.

Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) conseiller(ère), relations médias, positionnement corporatif et produits, afin de contribuer à des mandats d’envergure auprès de clients majeurs issus de secteurs variés, dont les affaires, les produits de consommation et le lifestyle.

La personne retenue aura l’occasion de travailler avec une équipe multidisciplinaire, des experts du bureau de Montréal et du réseau NATIONAL, ainsi qu’un portefeuille de clients évoluant dans des industries multiples.

Poste

Nous recherchons une personne capable de naviguer avec aisance entre créativité, rigueur et exécution concrète en relations médias, en positionnement de produits, et en collaborations avec des créateurs de contenu.

Au cœur des mandats, cette personne contribue à la réputation, à la visibilité et au positionnement de clients par l’entremise de programmes de relations médias, d’initiatives de positionnement de produits et de communications corporatives. Elle sait repérer les angles porteurs, structurer des approches claires et contribuer à transformer les priorités des clients en initiatives médiatiques pertinentes et percutantes.

Ce rôle s’adresse à une personne proactive, rigoureuse et curieuse, qui connaît bien l’écosystème médiatique québécois et canadien, et qui aime contribuer directement à la réalisation des mandats. La personne recherchée possède une plume stratégique et créative, suit de près l’actualité et les tendances, et sait évoluer dans des environnements rapides où la qualité, le jugement et la collaboration font toute la différence.

Responsabilités principales

Relations médias et positionnement

  • Contribuer au développement et au déploiement de programmes de relations médias produits et corporatifs pour des clients de différents secteurs
  • Identifier les angles, occasions médiatiques et approches de positionnement les plus pertinentes selon les objectifs des clients
  • Entretenir des relations régulières avec les médias, journalistes, chroniqueurs, créateurs de contenu et leaders d’opinion pertinents aux mandats
  • Assurer une connaissance active de l’écosystème médiatique au Québec et au Canada, notamment dans les secteurs des affaires, des produits de consommation et du lifestyle
  • Contribuer à la gestion de la réputation et du positionnement de produits, de marques et d’organisations dans des contextes variés

Exécution et gestion de mandats

  • Participer à la gestion de plusieurs programmes de communication simultanément, incluant les vigies, les relations médias, les suivis, les rapports, les partenariats et les livrables connexes
  • Assurer un suivi rigoureux des priorités, des échéanciers et de la qualité des livrables
  • Collaborer étroitement avec l’équipe en place et les autres expertises de NATIONAL selon les besoins des mandats
  • Contribuer activement à l’exécution des mandats, de la planification à la livraison, en s’impliquant là où cela crée le plus d’impact
  • Participer à l’identification d’opportunités de développement auprès de clients existants ou potentiels

Compétences

  • Minimum de 3 à 5 ans d’expérience en relations médias, positionnement corporatif et positionnement de produits, idéalement en agence
  • Diplôme universitaire en communication, relations publiques, marketing ou toute autre formation pertinente
  • Excellente connaissance de l’écosystème des médias au Québec et au Canada
  • Excellente maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral, afin de rédiger des communications adaptées aux différents publics, et de collaborer efficacement avec nos clients, collègues et compagnies sœurs au Canada et à l’international
  • Capacité à assurer un suivi rigoureux auprès des clients et à coordonner plusieurs mandats simultanément
  • Aisance avec les outils numériques et d’intelligence artificielle, les vigies médiatiques et les pratiques actuelles en communication

Qualités personnelles

  • Rigueur, sens des responsabilités et souci constant de la qualité
  • Réflexes aiguisés en relations médias et en gestion de projets
  • Curiosité, jugement et compréhension fine de l’actualité, des tendances et des environnements clients
  • Autonomie, proactivité et capacité à saisir rapidement les occasions
  • Capacité à gérer plusieurs projets simultanément, dont certains dans de courts échéanciers
  • Bonne résistance au stress et aisance dans des environnements rapides et évolutifs
  • Volonté de se développer au sein d’une organisation collaborative et ambitieuse

Ce que nous offrons

  • Poste à temps plein, du lundi au vendredi (remplacement de congé de maternité, avec possibilité de prolongation)
  • Horaire hybride : présentiel du lundi au jeudi, possibilité de télétravailler le vendredi
  • Programme mensuel de remboursement pour le transport en commun
  • Rabais sur l'abonnement saisonnier de BIXI en été
  • Assurance collective et compte de soins de santé
  • Accès au service Dialogue
  • Programmes de santé et de mieux-être
  • Environnement stimulant et humain, avec activités sociales variées
  • Accès à un centre d’entraînement dédié aux employés de l’immeuble ($)
  • Lieu de travail exceptionnel au cœur du centre-ville de Montréal

NATIONAL aide les organisations à faire face à des enjeux complexes en leur apportant de la clarté et du sens. Grâce à des analyses de pointe, des communications stratégiques et créatives, nous aidons les dirigeants et les organisations à communiquer avec détermination, à bâtir la confiance et à réaliser leurs objectifs les plus importants. Forts d'une équipe de 300 consultants, nous accompagnons un large éventail d'organisations œuvrant dans différents secteurs pour mieux comprendre les défis auxquels elles sont confrontées et saisir les occasions qui se présentent à elles.

Depuis 50 ans, NATIONAL est au cœur des enjeux et des secteurs qui comptent et contribue aux changements d'aujourd'hui et de demain. Chef de file canadien en communications, NATIONAL a des bureaux à Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Ottawa, Montréal, Québec, Saint-Jean, Halifax et St. John's. Son réseau comprend Time & Space, un chef de file en stratégie média, en analyse de données, en planification et en exécution.

Le Cabinet de relations publiques NATIONAL est une société d'AVENIR GLOBAL, la plus importante firme canadienne de communications, classée parmi les 25 plus importante au monde, disposant de bureaux dans 22 villes au Canada, aux États-Unis, en Europe et au Moyen-Orient. title: Director, Corporate Communications
description:
Director, Corporate Communications

Work location
Toronto, Ontario (hybrid).

About us

At NATIONAL, we are driven by purpose, creativity, and connection. For 50 years, our teams across Canada have helped organizations navigate change, build trust, and shape conversations that matter.

As one of Canada's largest independent communications consultancies, we partner with leading public and private organizations to solve complex business challenges through strategic communications, corporate affairs, capital markets expertise, and creative thinking.

Our Toronto team is looking for a senior communications leader with a strong background in financial communications, capital markets, and investor relations. This role is a good fit for someone who enjoys advising senior clients, making complicated business issues easier to understand, and working in a collaborative, fast-paced consulting environment.

If you are a trusted advisor who likes solving complex challenges, building lasting client relationships, and helping grow a dynamic practice, we would like to hear from you.

The role

This is a hands-on senior advisory opportunity for someone who wants to be both strategic and practical, commercially minded and collaborative, and comfortable advising clients when the stakes are high.

As Director, Corporate Communications, you will provide senior strategic counsel to executives, boards of directors, and investor relations teams. You will lead complex client mandates across corporate and financial communications, investor relations, capital markets initiatives, reputation management, crisis files, transaction communications, disclosure support, and special situations.

You will also play an important role in growing our practice. That means identifying and leading new business opportunities, expanding existing client relationships, mentoring colleagues, and connecting clients with the right expertise from across NATIONAL's practices and offices.

What you will do

As a senior member of the Toronto team, you will help clients communicate clearly in moments that matter to their business, their investors, their employees, their regulators, and other important stakeholders.

You will be expected to bring sound judgment, strong business instincts, and a clear understanding of how markets, media, investors, disclosure, and reputation intersect.

You will lead complex client mandates from planning through execution, making sure the work is thoughtful, high quality, delivered on time, and managed on budget.

You will build strong, enduring client relationships, identify opportunities to expand existing mandates, and lead new business opportunities that contribute to the growth of the Firm. You will also manage project planning, financial management, and resource allocation so that client objectives are met and the work runs smoothly.

You will collaborate with colleagues across NATIONAL's practices and offices to deliver integrated communications solutions that meet evolving client needs. You will mentor, coach, and develop team members, helping foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing culture.

You will stay close to capital markets trends, regulatory developments, and emerging communications practices so that your counsel is current, practical, and grounded in the realities of the market. You will also help strengthen NATIONAL's presence in the Canadian capital markets and financial communications community.

What you bring

You are a trusted advisor with a strong grounding in financial communications. You understand how to translate complex financial, market, and business issues into clear advice, credible messaging, and practical communications plans.

You are comfortable in senior rooms, including engaging with executives, boards, investor relations teams, legal advisors, bankers, analysts, and other stakeholders who are often part of high-profile, sensitive, or crisis-related mandates. You do not need to be a specialist in every situation, but you should bring the judgment and experience to know what matters, what questions to ask, and how to bring the right people together.

You likely bring:

  • 10+ years of experience in financial and corporate communications, capital markets, investor relations, strategic communications, or a consulting or corporate advisory environment.
  • Demonstrated experience providing strategic counsel to senior executives and leading complex communications or capital markets mandates, including crisis files.
  • Exceptional writing, presentation, and strategic communications skills, with the ability to develop compelling messaging across multiple channels.
  • Proven experience leading client relationships, managing budgets, and delivering complex projects in a fast-paced consulting environment.
  • A strong understanding of capital markets, financial communications, and the evolving media and digital landscape.
  • A bachelor's degree in Communications, Business, Finance, Public Relations, Journalism, or a related discipline. Experience advising publicly traded companies, investor relations teams or capital market participants is considered an asset. Familiarity with the Canadian capital markets landscape is also an asset.
  • Comfort using AI-enabled tools, for example, ChatGPT.
  • Nice to have: bilingualism in English and French.

How you work

You are strategic, but not removed from the work. You can see the larger picture, identify what matters, and turn advice into action. You are calm under pressure, clear in your counsel, and comfortable working in situations where the path forward is not always obvious.

You simplify complex issues, including financial and capital markets issues, and provide practical recommendations that clients can use. You bring a strong client-service mindset, build relationships naturally, and know how to manage stakeholders with confidence and discretion.

You are organized and comfortable managing budgets, timelines, resources, and tight deadlines. You can lead multiple priorities at once without losing sight of quality, detail, or client objectives.

You are collaborative, but highly self-sufficient. You can motivate teams, coach colleagues, contribute to an inclusive workplace, and draw on the strength of a national network when clients would benefit from additional expertise.

You are proactive, detail-oriented, adaptable, and committed to excellent client service.

What we offer

  • A hybrid work environment and a supportive, collegial Toronto office culture.
  • Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits.
  • Opportunities to work on high-profile mandates with leading organizations across sectors.
  • Professional development, coaching, and growth opportunities within a national team.
  • Occasional travel as required by client and team needs.

Expected Compensation

The expected salary for this role is $103,500 - $115,000 CAD. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and internal equity.

How to apply

Qualified candidates are invited to apply by submitting a resume and a brief cover letter outlining their interest in the role, relevant experience, and fit for a senior financial communications, corporate communications, and capital markets advisory role. If you are up for a new challenge to join Canada's PR Firm, we would like to hear from you.

title: Director, Public Affairs and Regional Lead
description:
About us

At NATIONAL, we are driven by purpose, creativity, and connection. For 50 years, our teams across Canada have been delivering strategic communications expertise that helps organizations shape conversations that matter.

NATIONAL is seeking a senior communications leader for Newfoundland and Labrador. While this opportunity is currently posted at the Director level, we welcome interest from experienced communications professionals and seasoned executives, with level, scope, and title to be considered based on experience, capability, and market presence.

This is a rare opportunity for someone who knows the province, understands how decisions are made, and can move confidently between public affairs, government relations, corporate communications, and marketing conversations.

Our Newfoundland and Labrador presence is an important part of our Atlantic and national network. We work with clients across sectors, regions, and issues, helping them navigate complex environments, build trust, and communicate with clarity. With a strong local and regional foundation and access to the full strength of NATIONAL’s offices across Canada, this role offers the opportunity to help shape what comes next in one of the country’s most distinctive and strategically important markets.

The role

This is a hands-on, senior market-building opportunity for someone who wants to be both strategic and practical, visible and grounded, independent and deeply connected to a national team. We are looking for an entrepreneurial leader who can help grow NATIONAL’s presence in Newfoundland and Labrador while contributing to client work across Atlantic Canada and the broader NATIONAL network. Whether you’re currently living in the region, or looking to return home, the ideal candidate is deeply connected to the province. They understand the local business, political, and community landscape, and they bring the judgment, presence, and credibility to advise executives, engage stakeholders, and represent NATIONAL in the market.

Our office is located within the Board of Trade in St. John’s, offering a strong connection to the local business community and an energizing space for client work, collaboration, and growth.

What you will do

As a key member of the Atlantic and Canadian Advisory and Public Affairs practice team, you will provide senior counsel to clients navigating complex communications, public affairs, and reputational challenges. Our roster of clients are closely connected to the biggest opportunities and challenges NL is facing. You will bring a strong understanding of government, business, community, and media environments in Newfoundland and Labrador, with particular interest in sectors such as energy, defense, economic development, healthcare and other areas shaping the future of the province. Ideally, your experience and skillset can contribute to client needs outside of NL and outside of Atlantic Canada.

You will help lead and grow client relationships, identify new opportunities, and connect clients with the right expertise from across NATIONAL. You will be expected to work independently, think strategically, and manage mandates with confidence, while also knowing when and how to bring in colleagues from other offices and practice areas.

You will represent NATIONAL in the Newfoundland and Labrador market, helping to strengthen our visibility, relationships, and reputation. You will be comfortable in a boardroom, at a community event, in a government relations discussion, or in a marketing strategy conversation. You do not need to be a specialist in every discipline, but you should be an integrated thinker who understands how public affairs, communications, marketing, stakeholder engagement, and reputation intersect. In this role, you will be part of the broader.

What you bring

You are someone excited about local and regional connectivity and are a trusted advisor with strong judgment, sound instincts, and the ability to build relationships across sectors. You are self-motivated and credible with executives, comfortable with elected officials and senior public servants, and able to speak naturally with people from a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives.

You likely bring:

  • Senior experience in public affairs, government relations, strategic communications, crisis communications, public relations, or a related professional services environment
  • Strong knowledge of Newfoundland and Labrador’s political, business, community, and media landscape
  • Experience or strong familiarity with sectors such as energy, defense, infrastructure, natural resources, economic development, or other regulated or high-profile industries
  • The ability to lead client relationships, provide wise counsel, and manage complex mandates with limited day-to-day oversight
  • A practical understanding of marketing and integrated communications, with the ability to contribute meaningfully to broader brand, reputation, and campaign conversations
  • Strong writing, presentation, facilitation, and relationship-building skills
  • An entrepreneurial mindset and interest in helping grow NATIONAL’s presence in Newfoundland and Labrador
  • The ability to collaborate across offices, especially with Atlantic Canada, Ottawa, and other teams across the NATIONAL network
  • A degree or equivalent experience in communications, public relations, political science, business, public policy, journalism, marketing, or a related field

How you work

You are strategic, but not removed from the work. You can see the larger picture, identify what matters, and turn advice into action. You are calm under pressure, clear in your counsel, and comfortable working in situations where the path forward is not always obvious. You have good judgement.

You build trust easily. You are good in a room, thoughtful in your approach, and able to move between senior executives, community leaders, public officials, colleagues, and clients with confidence and respect. You are a good writer and easily adjust to different mediums and audiences. You are collaborative, but highly self-sufficient. You can build something without needing a large local team around you, and you know how to draw on the strength of a national network when clients would benefit from additional expertise.

You are values-driven, discreet, adaptable, and committed to excellent client service.

What we offer

  • The opportunity to help shape NATIONAL’s value as a consultancy in Newfoundland and Labrador
  • A senior, market-facing role with room to grow based on experience, capability, and ambition
  • A connected national platform with strong Atlantic Canadian collaboration
  • Exposure to meaningful client work across public affairs, government relations, corporate communications, marketing, and reputation
  • A dynamic, entrepreneurial environment with the support of one of Canada’s most respected communications consultancies
  • Competitive compensation, commensurate with level and experience
  • Hybrid flexibility with an expectation of meaningful presence in the St. John’s market
  • A commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in all that we do

How to apply

Qualified candidates are invited to apply by submitting a resume and a brief cover letter outlining their interest in the role, connection to Newfoundland and Labrador, and relevant experience.

title: Senior Consultant, Public Affairs and Government Relations
description:
About us

At NATIONAL, we are proud to be Canada’s leading public relations firm, bringing together a coast-to-coast network of public affairs experts. In Toronto, our Public Affairs and Government Relations team partners with clients across a wide range of sectors to design, activate, and manage strategies that resonate with audiences and deliver measurable impact. As our team continues to grow, we are seeking a consultant with a passion for strategic communications, public affairs, government relations and, above and beyond, exceptional client service.

The role

As a Senior Consultant on NATIONAL’s Public Affairs and Government Relations team in Toronto, you will help clients understand and navigate complex political, regulatory and reputational environments. You will support high-profile mandates across sectors, helping to turn current events, policy developments and stakeholder dynamics into practical strategies that advance client goals.

This role is ideal for someone with strong political instincts, excellent client service skills and the ability to manage multiple moving pieces in a fast-paced agency environment. You may come from a public affairs agency, a political office, government, corporate communications or another client-facing advisory role.

Key responsibilities

  • Serve as the day-to-day, client-facing manager for accounts across multiple industry sectors
  • Collaborate with senior communications and public affairs leaders to deliver expert counsel and exceptional service
  • Design, manage, and execute impactful municipal and provincial government relations programs as well as stakeholder engagement and advocacy campaigns
  • Lead and support reputation management programs, issues and crisis management, and communications campaigns (earned, owned, and paid media strategies)
  • Monitor and analyze evolving political, economic, and social issues; proactively propose strategies to advance client goals
  • Oversee account management, including project work plans and budgets
  • Contribute to practice and Firm-wide business development initiatives, with a focus on issues/crisis management, reputation management, campaign strategy and activation, public engagement, and stakeholder relations
  • Work with colleagues across NATIONAL practices and offices to deliver integrated communications services

  • Three to six years of experience in public affairs, government relations, strategic communications, political offices, consulting, government or a related environment
  • Strong understanding of Ontario politics, municipal government and/or public policy
  • Post-secondary degree in public relations, political science, business administration, public administration, or a related field
  • Agency experience, political staff experience or experience supporting senior decision-makers considered a strong asset
  • Excellent writing, research and presentation skills
  • Strong client service instincts, including responsiveness, organization, judgment and attention to detail
  • Ability to monitor political, media and stakeholder developments and translate them into client-relevant insights
  • Comfortable managing multiple files, deadlines and relationships at once
  • Entrepreneurial, curious and motivated to help grow the practice

Abilities

  • Sound judgment and critical thinking, with the ability to assess complex situations and recommend practical courses of action
  • Ability to anticipate needs, identify emerging opportunities and challenges, and proactively bring forward solutions
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities, with the ability to work effectively with clients, colleagues and external stakeholders
  • Ability to collaborate effectively as part of a team while taking ownership of work and driving assignments forward independently
  • Adaptability and comfort working in a fast-paced environment where priorities and circumstances can change quickly
  • Commitment to continuous learning and staying current on political, policy, communications and industry developments

What we offer

  • A collaborative, entrepreneurial workplace culture that values curiosity, innovation and teamwork
  • The opportunity to work directly with senior advisors, clients and decision-makers on high-profile files at the intersection of business, politics, media and public opinion
  • Meaningful responsibility, mentorship and opportunities to accelerate your career in public affairs and government relations
  • Exposure to a diverse portfolio of clients, industries and public policy issues across Canada
  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits

Expected Compensation

  • The expected salary for this role is $77,000-$87,500 CAD. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and internal equity.
